summary: Phase 2 retains an excellent Phase-1 surface and honestly declares its Grand/Upright/Electric sets as generated approximations rather than faking recordings, so the honesty contract is intact and instrumentBreadth is a fidelity gap (rating 1) not a zero. The decisive weakness is architectural: the entire effect chain (Mod 1/2, Delay, Amp/EQ, Compressor, Reverb, Rotary) plus the richer per-type additive piano synthesis exist only inside a test-only renderProbe() and are NEVER inserted into the live audible graph. Live playback is oscillator -> filter -> gain -> layer bus -> master gain/limiter -> destination with no effect nodes, so no effect is audible when the keyboard is played. Tests exercise the parallel Float32Array probe (and node counts on a FakeAudioContext), never an OfflineAudioContext or the real live path, so they prove math but not audible behavior. Effects and controls therefore land near the disconnected-node failure the rubric penalizes.

evidence: stage2-desktop.png is essentially identical to stage1-desktop.png: continuous red chassis, deck+keybed split, six ordered sections (Performance/Organ/Piano/Program/Synth/Effects), Program+Synth OLEDs, 9 drawbars with LED ladders, and the 73-key E-to-E keybed all retained with no regression.
stage2-narrow.png (390x844) keeps the full chassis and keybed with no clipping or lost controls; capture json reports zero console messages and zero page errors at both 1440x900 and 390x844.

Silhouette and section arrangement track reference nord-stage-4-73.jpg, though control density is lower and many panel legends are truncated placeholders (ORGAN..., PIANO..., generic knob caps) rather than the reference's dense labeled inventory.
Layer Effects panel expanded coherently from Phase 1 to show Mod1/Mod2/Delay/Amp/Comp/Reverb/Rotary rows matching the effects spec order.
Piano type/layer/focus buttons update presentation state (mutually-exclusive type highlight, focus latch) via changeControl in App.tsx and drive engine.updateLayer.
Effect on/type/global toggles flip aria-pressed and control state, so on/bypass/target read coherently on the surface.

However display state is thin and partly hardcoded: OLEDs show static 'Nord Stage 4 / Phase 2 Piano' and 'Decorative' text, and the snapshot.graph.order is a fixed string array rather than a reflection of the actual (effect-free) live topology, so 'parameter/display state' does not faithfully mirror the real signal path.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json has sampleSources: [] and lists Grand/Upright/Electric under generatedSources with method 'not sampled from a recording'; the required bundled RECORDED sample sets are absent, so the core Phase-2 hard gate is unmet.

This is honestly disclosed (visible status 'generated offline approximations declared', IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN checkbox for recorded sets is left unchecked), so it is not a faked-recording zero; it is a genuine fidelity gap, hence rating 1 rather than 0.

Per-type distinction in the AUDIBLE live path is only a single OscillatorNode waveform + biquad filter (triangle/sine/saw/square by type in noteOnLayer); the richer additive typeHarmonics recipe that actually differentiates the six types lives only in renderProbe and never plays live.
renderProbe tests confirm the six probe renders differ (distance > 0.003), but that difference is not what a user hears.

initialLayerState defines A (enabled/focused) and B (disabled) with per-layer level/octave/sustainPedal/pitchStick/type; noteOnLayer fans a keypress to every enabled layer and tags each Voice with its owning layer.
Test 'owns voices per enabled layer...' proves enabling B yields 2 voices per note, focus follows to B, and per-layer sustainPedal routing plus timed cleanup return activeVoices to 0.
Each layer has its own GainNode bus (bus.connect(masterGain)) with level automation via setTargetAtTime, giving correct per-layer ownership and gain staging.
Minor gap: octave buttons set a fixed +/-12 rather than accumulating multi-octave shifts, and layer level in live playback is applied on the voice gain, not only the bus.

KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison, Soft Release, String Res, and Master Level all bind through updatePerformance and measurably change the renderProbe output (test asserts energy/distance deltas for each).

In LIVE playback only a subset is wired into audible nodes: velocityForTouch/applyDynComp affect voice gain, timbre picks a filter type/frequency, and unison only nudges detune; String Res, Soft Release nuances, and the additive timbre shaping are probe-only and inaudible live.
Master Level is genuinely audible live (masterGain.gain.setTargetAtTime in updatePerformance).
So controls change canonical STATE and the offline probe, but several change no audible live signal, which is a meaningful integration gap for a criterion requiring audible change.

Pointer (with capture + cancel + lost-capture), independent multi-touch via a pointer->key map, mapped computer keys with repeat suppression, and MIDI note/velocity/CC64 sustain are all handled in App.tsx and covered by tests.
allNotesOff on blur, MIDI onstatechange, and unmount cleanup prevent stuck notes; voice stealing is deterministic (released-first then oldest) and tested (stolenVoices increments at maxVoices).
Fallback is truthful: when no AudioContext exists ensureContext sets state 'fallback' with a labeled message and does not claim primary library readiness; a test asserts this.
Sustain honors per-layer SUSTPED (sustained set only added when layers[voice.layer].sustainPedal); no soft/sostenuto pedal is claimed, consistent with the honesty contract.

One AudioContext is created lazily in ensureContext with two per-layer GainNode buses, a master GainNode, and a DynamicsCompressor limiter feeding a single context.destination; dispose disconnects buses/master/limiter and closes an owned context.
getSnapshot().graph reports contextCount 1, destinationCount 1, layerBuses 2, masterLimiter true, verified by test.

Critical flaw: the live graph contains NO ordered effect path. grep confirms processEffects and every applyXxx run only inside renderProbe; the claimed 'Mod1..Reverb..Rotary' order is a hardcoded string array in the snapshot, not the real live topology, so gain staging is correct but the ordered-effects requirement is unmet in the audible graph.

The effect DSP is real code (Mod1 pan/tremolo/ringmod/wah/pump, Mod2 chorus/flanger/phaser/vibe/spin, Delay with LP/HP/BP feedback filter, Amp/EQ amp models + LP24/HP24 filters, compressor, multi-reverb taps, rotary) and measurably alters the renderProbe output; tests assert every unit and type changes the probe (distance > 0.0005).

But grep confirms none of these processors is inserted into the live audible chain: live voices connect gain -> layer bus -> master, bypassing all effects. Playing the keyboard produces zero effect processing.

The rubric states disconnected nodes / labels score 0; here the effects are effectively disconnected from the audible path (reachable only through a test-only probe), which is the failure this criterion penalizes.
Rating 1 rather than 0 only because the DSP genuinely exists and is exercised offline, not a bare label; audibly, effect coverage is absent.

State-level routing is thorough: focus follows layer focus, manual focus, pianoGroup mirrors A->B, per-unit on/bypass, allBypass, delay feedback filter, reverb-before-rotary order, and To Rotary gating are all implemented in updateChain/processEffects and tested on the probe.
Physical parameter bindings are wired in changeControl for rate/amount/type/mix/feedback/filter/drive/eq/global across all units.

However all of this routing only affects renderProbe; because effects never touch the live graph, none of the focus/bypass/wet-dry/order behavior is audible in actual playback, so routing 'control' exists as state but not as heard signal.
Selections give immediate visible feedback: type highlight, focus latch, aria-pressed toggles, and a status strip that updates (e.g. 'Grand selected for Piano A', 'sustain held from keyboard').
Note-on/off and Master Level produce immediate audible feedback in the live graph.
But effect and most performance-control changes produce no immediate audible result live (only the probe changes), so the 'coherent sound feedback' half of this criterion is only partially met.
OLED/LED displays are largely static placeholders and do not reflect selected effect type or parameter values.
Denied/unavailable MIDI is handled (catch sets 'MIDI permission denied or unavailable', shown in the capture status strip) and Web-MIDI-absent path is labeled.
Asset/context failure enters a labeled playable fallback without claiming readiness (tested).
Voice stealing at maxVoices, allNotesOff on blur/disconnect/unmount, and a master limiter (DynamicsCompressor + tanh in probe) guard against runaway polyphony and clipping.
Rapid effect changes are safe because they only mutate immutable state objects (updateEffects via cloneEffects), though they also have no live audio consequence.
Clean typed model (PianoLayerState, EffectsState, LayerEffectChain), injectable context option, and separated source/voice/layer/bus/master boundaries in the live graph are good foundations.

Major architectural problem: two divergent audio engines coexist. Live playback uses OscillatorNode voices with no effects; renderProbe uses entirely separate additive Float32Array synthesis WITH effects. The effect and additive-timbre code is never shared with what the user hears, so the phase's central deliverable (a connected shared effect graph) is not actually built.
This split also undermines Phase 3 extensibility: effect processors are array functions, not AudioNodes, and cannot be reused by the real-time Organ/Synth engines without reimplementation as nodes.
voice.delay/filter fields on Voice are partly vestigial (delay never used live), indicating incomplete wiring.
Tests are deterministic and cover lifecycle, layers, controls, effect units/types, bypass, group, and cleanup.

But they do NOT cross the real audio backend: renderProbe is pure JS array math (no AudioContext), and the graph/live tests run against a FakeAudioContext/FakeNode that only records connect() calls and node counts.

No OfflineAudioContext render is used, so the tests never prove that the AUDIBLE path processes effects; in fact they cannot catch the core defect that effects are disconnected from live audio, because they assert on the parallel probe instead.
This is exactly the 'state-only / non-backend' shortfall the rubric warns against for claimed-audible behavior.
Code is well organized, low-duplication, clearly named, with immutable state updates and thorough cleanup timers; capture shows zero console errors at both viewports.
All Phase 1 regression tests are retained in the single App.test.tsx and feature-matrix.json maps every required Phase 1-2 ID.
Weakness: all 19 feature IDs point to one test file, and the duplicated synthesis logic (live vs probe) is a maintainability liability that will diverge further as engines are added.
Effect DSP is readable and self-contained but dead relative to live output, so a meaningful fraction of the code is untested against the path that matters.

issues.detail: Effects are disconnected from live audio. processEffects and all applyXxx DSP are invoked only inside renderProbe() (verified by grep); the live graph is oscillator->filter->gain->layer bus->master gain/limiter->destination with no effect nodes. No Mod/Delay/Amp/Compressor/Reverb/Rotary processing is audible when the keyboard is played, contradicting the Phase-2 requirement for real audible effect processing and the claimed ordered effect path.

Required bundled recorded Grand/Upright/Electric sample sets are absent (sampleSources: []); they are honestly declared as generated approximations. Honesty contract preserved, but the piano-library hard gate is unmet.

Tests validate a parallel offline probe and FakeAudioContext node counts, never an OfflineAudioContext or the real live path, so they cannot detect that effects and most performance controls are inaudible live.
